[34mInvestigated:[0m The Scheduler job-selection path in schedule/__init__.py: run_pending filters on Job.should_run, run_all ignores should_run, get_next_run and idle_seconds read next_run across all tagged jobs, and Job.should_run compares only the current time to next_run. The existing tag-based get_jobs and clear methods, the module-level wrappers, the test file conventions, and the docs/reference.rst autofunction list were also examined.

[33mLearned:[0m Because should_run compares only against next_run, a job skipped while paused keeps a past next_run and runs once on the first run_pending after resume. run_all bypasses should_run entirely, so pause needed an explicit decision there. Without excluding paused jobs from get_next_run and idle_seconds, a paused overdue job would give a negative idle_seconds and could make a sleep loop spin.

[32mCompleted:[0m Added Scheduler.pause(tag) and Scheduler.resume(tag), backed by a _paused_tags set initialized in __init__. run_pending skips any job with a paused tag, including multi-tag jobs where any tag is paused. get_next_run, next_run and idle_seconds ignore paused jobs and return None when all matching jobs are paused. clear(tag) un-pauses that tag, and clear() empties the pause set. Module-level pause and resume wrappers were added, and docs/reference.rst gained autofunction entries for both. Five tests were added to test_schedule.py covering tag pause and resume, jobs added later, multi-tag jobs, unknown and repeated resume calls, next_run/idle_seconds/run_all with paused jobs, and clear resetting pause. The full suite passes with 88 tests. Changes are in three modified files and are not committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m Commit the pause/resume changes to schedule/__init__.py, test_schedule.py, and docs/reference.rst. Build the autoclass docs to confirm the new pause and resume entries render. Await the user's decision on whether run_all should respect paused tags, since it currently still runs them.

[36mNotes:[0m A design choice in the pause semantics needs confirmation: run_all still runs paused jobs, which the docstring documents as intentional. The rationale given was that run_all means "run everything now", but this could surprise maintenance-window users. Pausing also applies to jobs tagged after the pause call, which the user has not explicitly confirmed. The earlier commit a5d1ad4 for get_jobs_for is the most recent committed work, and this pause/resume work sits on top of it uncommitted.
